title: Coordinates Lookup Tool: Map, Record and Facts
description: Look up a coordinate pair fully with the Coordinates Lookup Tool — map position, administrative record, antipode heading and equator distance. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, one paste of 40.7580, −73.9855 returns the map pin, the address record, the distance to the equator (about 4,514 km of latitude) and the antipode heading — the whole dossier on two numbers.
quick_answer: The Coordinates Lookup Tool does the whole job for a coordinate pair: it shows where the point is on the map, reads its administrative record, and derives facts like the antipode heading and equator distance. Paste the coordinates — or click instead — and read the point's complete dossier.

body.t: A pair arrives from a log, a photo, a colleague. The dossier answers what/where/whose in one paste — deeper fields live in the
Standing at a claimed point? Compare the device's pair against the lookup's record before trusting either.
Coordinates in a report deserve their context — place record plus derived facts turns naked numbers into a defensible entry.
Antipode headings and equator distances are the geography-party facts. This page computes them properly instead of letting you guess.

Times Square's latitude of 40.758° is about 4,514 km of meridian arc from the equator — computed from the latitude with WGS84's degree length (the WGS84 meridian arc for that latitude, as the tool's method states).
Dig straight through from Times Square and you surface in the Indian Ocean southwest of Australia — the lookup's antipode facts give the heading and the far point's coordinates for the map.

faq: What do I get beyond the address?
The derived layer: antipode heading and point, equator distance and the map context — facts computed from the coordinates themselves, alongside the record's address fields.
Can I click instead of typing?
Yes — the map accepts clicks as happily as pastes; the dossier builds for the clicked point identically.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84 — paste GPS pairs as they come.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
The dossier's record fields saturate quickly (the city is the city at 3 decimals); derived facts keep the input's figures honestly.
Can I copy the result into GIS software?
Coordinates and fields both copy — the dossier is designed as the paste source for notes, reports and GIS attributes.
Ocean points?
The record thins to little or nothing, while derived facts (antipode, equator distance) still compute — the page shows which kind of answer each field is.
The record disagrees with my other app.
Different data vintages and providers. The lookup reports the open record; where it matters, the disagreement itself is the finding.
Batch lookups?
One pair at a time — the dossier is a per-point instrument. Lists belong to the Batch Geocoder.
Antipode on land?
Most antipodes are ocean (the planet is mostly water, and land antipodes are rare) — the lookup reports whichever yours is, land naming included where the record reaches.
Equator distance versus latitude degrees?
Same fact, two dresses: degrees for charts, kilometres for humans. The lookup gives the kilometre reading.
Is my lookup stored?
No — the pair is processed for the answer, not kept.
